See How Much Money You Could Be Making

Example: $20,000/mo in ad spend on Google Ads = $4,000/mo management fee. The $1,500 minimum fee per platform acts as a floor, covering your first $7,500 in ad spend. Once you spend over $7,500, the 20% rate naturally takes over.

One question we get a lot: if we're paid on a percentage of spend, why wouldn't we just push you to spend more forever? Honestly, we don't. You set the budget. We don't recommend increasing it until the numbers justify it. And the fee is capped at $15,000/mo anyway. As you grow, we grow. That's kind of the whole point.

Pricing Questions

How much does Creekside Marketing charge?
Our management fee is a percentage of your ad spend: 20% up to $30k, 15% from $30k to $60k, and 10% above $60k per platform. There's a $1,500 monthly minimum per platform, and total fees are capped at $15,000 per month.
What's included in the management fee?
Everything required to make your ads succeed: campaign management, landing pages, ad creatives, copywriting, conversion tracking setup including server-side tracking and CRM integration, conversion rate optimization, live reporting, bi-weekly reports, and monthly strategy calls. There are no separate line items.
Are there any long-term contracts?
No. There are no long-term contracts, and your first 7 days are covered by a full money-back guarantee.
Do you charge per platform?
Yes. The fee is calculated per platform. If we manage both Google Ads and Meta Ads, each platform has its own tiered rate and $1,500 minimum, and your combined total is still capped at $15,000 per month.
What guarantees do you offer?
Two. First, a 7-day money-back guarantee: meet the team, see how we work, and if we're not the right fit within your first 7 days, you get a full refund. Second, a 90-day performance promise: if we don't improve your ROAS within 90 days, we work for free until we do.
Which plan should I choose?
There's only one pricing structure, and it works at every budget level. The percentage rate decreases as your spend grows (20% to $30k, 15% to $60k, 10% above), so the more you invest, the lower your effective rate.
